description: Independent source-scope ordinary-language development set: 10 turns in 5 two-turn correlated scenarios. Synthetic project facts are explicit; no1070 attributes are inferred.

scope.modelPromptIsolation: Do not send checks,references,evaluationMetadata or keys to retrieval/writer/verifier; only questions,project facts and ordinary prior conversation.

questions: For a new NYC building under the 2022 codes, the crawl space is 1,500 square feet. With ordinary openings providing cross ventilation and no exception, what net vent opening area is required?
Keep that crawl space, but cover the ground with a Class I vapor retarder and retain openings providing cross ventilation. What reduced net opening area does that exception allow?
checks: 10 square feet net: 1 square foot per 150 square feet of crawl space.
1 square foot net: the Class I vapor-retarder plus cross-ventilation exception permits 1/1,500 of the under-floor area.

evaluationMetadata.scenarioProvenance: Explicit fictional test facts; no real project inference
sourceKeyNotes: No flood hazard, mechanical ventilation or conditioned-space exception is being invoked.

questions: For a NYC medical clinic under the 2022 Plumbing Code, may its clinical sink in a soiled utility room also count as the service sink?
Then can staff dispose of urine or fecal waste in the ordinary service sink instead?
checks: No. A clinical sink serving a soiled utility room cannot substitute for or be used as a service sink.
No. A service sink cannot be used to dispose of urine, fecal matter or other human waste.

questions: Under the 2022 NYC mechanical rules, an outdoor unit at grade sits on a level concrete pad extending 2 inches above adjacent grade. The manufacturer permits this support. Is that pad height enough?
If I suspend the unit instead, would 5 inches above adjacent grade satisfy the minimum suspended clearance?
checks: No. The slab or other approved supporting material must extend at least 3 inches above adjoining grade. Manufacturer instructions also apply.
No. The alternative suspended installation must be at least 6 inches above adjoining grade.

evaluationMetadata.scenarioProvenance: Explicit fictional test facts; no real project inference
sourceKeyNotes: Only grade-support height is asked, not full weather/flood/listing approval.

questions: For a new NYC commercial kitchen under the 2022 Fuel Gas Code, a gas range is on casters for routine cleaning. May its flexible gas connector be an ordinary fixed-appliance connector rather than one listed for movable appliances?
If I choose a connector listed for movable appliances, can I leave it exposed where rolling the range can damage it?
checks: No. For this commercial cooking appliance on casters, the connector must be listed to ANSI Z21.69/CSA 6.16 and NSF/ANSI 169, or use the permitted rigid-pipe-and-fittings alternative; an ordinary fixed-appliance connector alone is not the specified connector.
No. Flexible connectors for movable appliances must be installed and protected against physical damage according to manufacturer instructions.

sourceKeyNotes: An answer may correctly mention the Item 1 rigid metallic piping alternative. Do not grade as requiring a flexible connector in every design.

questions: Under the NYC Fire Code, our office building has a stationary fuel-oil-fired boiler. A dry-chemical 20-B:C extinguisher is 40 feet away by travel distance. Is that rating and distance combination sufficient for this equipment?
If I keep the 40-foot travel distance and use a dry-chemical 40-B:C extinguisher, does the increased-distance option allow it?
checks: No. The 20-B:C dry-chemical option must be within 30 feet. The rule applies outside Group R-3.
Yes for this rating/distance condition. A dry-chemical extinguisher rated at least 40-B:C allows travel distance up to 50 feet; other placement and maintenance rules still apply.
